draft.text:
For weeks JobMatch told me a job was an 8 out of 10 fit. Helpful, but it never told me why.

So I built the ATS score panel. Now instead of a single number, I get a visual breakdown of how my CV actually matches the job description.

It shows me which keywords from the posting made it into my CV and which ones I quietly missed. The skills I thought were obvious but never spelled out. The phrasing a real applicant tracking system would be scanning for.

The first time I ran it on my own CV, I had a small reality check. I was describing a full Opera Cloud migration in language no machine would ever connect to the role I was applying for.

That is the part I keep relearning. The work was real. The translation was missing.

This pairs with the manual job description paste I kept on purpose. I only run roles I have actually chosen, and now the panel tells me how far my real experience is from how that role is written.

It is still rough. The keyword matching is simpler than I want, and I have a long list of things to refine before it feels finished.

But it does the one thing I needed when I started this whole project. It turns a vague feeling of not being good enough into something specific I can fix.
